title: 3.1 Introduction to Ethical Decision Making 🧩 (የስነ-ምግባር ውሳኔ አሰጣጥ መግቢያ)
content: 📌 እንኳን ደህና መጣህ ውድ ወንድሜ! ውዷ እህቴ! 👋 የተወደደውና የተባረከው የትምህርት ጊዜያችን ስኬታማ እንዲሆን በሙሉ ፍቅርና በጎ ምኞት እመኛለሁ! ይህ የምዕራፍ 3 አካል 1 (Chapter 3 Part 1) ነው። በጥንቃቄ ተከታተለሉኝ👇👇 The Need for Moral Decisions: • Individuals constantly face choices between satisfying, giving up, or postponing desires. • Standard of Right vs. Wrong: Deciding what is right versus wrong is a perpetual human puzzle. Primary Functions of Morality: 1. Personal Guidance: Provides standards to make correct decisions when facing ethical choices. 2. Social Order & Conflict Resolution: Provides acceptable rules to prevent or resolve conflicts and promotes peaceful, cooperative living. Role of Ethical Theories: • When complex problems arise, ethical theories help us reflect on the meaning and end of morality, guiding our actions and moral judgments. 👉 ውድ ወንድሜ፣ የሰው ልጅ በዕለት ተዕለት ሕይወቱ የትኛውን ፍላጎቱን ማሟላት እንዳለበት እና የትኛውን ማቆየት ወይም መተው እንዳለበት የመወሰን ፈተና ይገጥመዋል። የስነ-ምግባር (Morality) ዋነኛ ጥቅም ሰዎች ትክክለኛ ውሳኔ እንዲወስኑ መምራት እና በህብረተሰብ ውስጥ ግጭቶች እንዳይፈጠሩ የሚያስችሉ የጋራ ህጎችን ማቅረብ ነው። 💡 Exam Focus: Remember the two main functions of morality: guiding individual decisions and maintaining social order/resolving conflicts!

title: 3.3 Making Ethical Decisions: Intrinsic vs. Instrumental Values ⚖️
content: 📌 Understanding Good and Bad: • The moral quality of our actions depends on our notions of "Good", "Bad", "Right", and "Wrong". Two Categories of Goodness: • Instrumental Good: Things considered good because of what they lead to or achieve (they serve as instruments to attain other desirable ends). • Intrinsic Good: Things valuable in themselves for their own sake/nature, not merely as a means to get something else. Instrumental vs. Intrinsic Evil/Bad: • Practices can also be instrumentally or intrinsically bad. • Examples of societal evils in Ethiopia: Female Genital Mutilation (FGM), early marriage, abduction, ignorance, poverty, corruption, and murder. 👉 ነገሮችን በጥሩ እና በክፉ ስንመድባቸው በሁለት ይከፈላሉ፦ • ኢንስትሩሜንታል (Instrumental Good): ለአንድ ሌላ ጥሩ ነገር ማድረሻ መሳሪያ ስለሆኑ ብቻ ጥሩ የሚባሉ። • ኢንትሪንሲክ (Intrinsic Good): በራሳቸው ማንነትና ባህሪ ውድና ጥሩ የሆኑ ነገሮች። በተመሳሳይ መልኩ እንደ ኤች.አይ.ቪ፣ ድህነት፣ የሴቶች ግረዛ እና ሙስና ያሉ ነገሮች በህብረተሰቡ ውስጥ ጎጂና መወገድ ያለባቸው እኩይ ተግባራት ናቸው። 💡 Exam Hint: Be ready to classify actions/objects as Instrumental Good (means to an end) vs. Intrinsic Good (end in itself)!

title: Tasks of Ethical Reasoning & Value Dilemmas 🔍
content: 📌 Key Tasks of Ethical Reasoning: 1. Analyzing Values & Claims: Critically evaluating personal/societal values regarding obligations to others. - Sanctity of Life: The intrinsic value of being alive. - Quality of Life: The moral significance of positive experiences vs. suffering. - Autonomy: Respecting an individual's personal choices (e.g., end-of-life care decisions). 2. Evaluating Reasons & Arguments: Assessing whether justifications for actions are backed by sound evidence and logical reasoning. Nature of Ethical Problems: • Unlike scientific tasks (e.g., measuring blood pressure), ethical values like virtue or courage are complex and abstract. • Ethical issues are rarely clear-cut black-and-white; ethics seeks out the "grey areas" to offer analytical tools rather than lecturing people. 👉 የስነ-ምግባር ሙግት (Ethical Reasoning) ዋና ተግባር የያዝናቸውን እሴቶች መመርመር እና ለድርጊታችን የምንሰጣቸውን ምክንያቶች ሚዛናዊነት መገምገም ነው። የስነ-ምግባር ችግሮች እንደ ሳይንሳዊ ምርመራዎች ግልጽና ቀላል አይደሉም፤ ይልቁንም ውስብስብ የሆኑ የሕይወት ቅራኔዎችን በጥልቀት ለመረዳት የሚያስችሉ መሳሪያዎችን ይሰጠናል። 💡 Exam Focus: Ethics does not just dictate right and wrong; its primary purpose is to provide framework tools for navigating complex gray areas through reasonable reflection.

title: 3.3.1 Ethical Principles and Values of Moral Judgments 📜
content: 📌 Everyday Rules vs. Deep Philosophical Ethics: • Most people use practical "rules of thumb" in daily life (e.g., "it is wrong to steal", "help those in need"). • Complex life situations put simple rules to the test: - Is capital punishment wrong? - Is self-defense killing acceptable? - Are abortion or euthanasia morally permissible? Role of Philosophers: • Daily rules often fail when facing complex moral dilemmas. • Philosophers build systematic, rational theoretical frameworks to provide coherent solutions applicable across society. 👉 አብዛኛው ሰው በዕለት ተዕለት ሕይወቱ እንደ "መስረቅ ስህተት ነው" ወይም "ተቸጋሪን መረዳት ተገቢ ነው" ያሉ ቀላል ህጎችን ይከተላል። ነገር ግን እንደ ሞት ቅጣት፣ ፅንስ ማቋረጥ ወይም እራስን ለመከላከል ሰውን መግደል ያሉ ውስብስብ ጥያቄዎች ሲመጡ እነዚህ ህጎች ብቻቸውን በቂ አይደሉም። ስለዚህ የፍልስፍና ስነ-ምግባር አስተማማኝ ስርዓቶችን ይገነባል። 💡 Exam Hint: Everyday rules of thumb are helpful, but complex moral dilemmas require structured theoretical frameworks to evaluate actions rationally.

title: 3.3.2 Moral Intuitions, Critical Reasoning & Conscience 🧠
content: 📌 The Formation of Conscience: • Empathy: Provides feelings of identification with others. • Moral Sentiments: Emotional responses derived from empathy. • Moral Principles: Formed when we apply ethical reasoning to our moral sentiments. • Moral Conscience: The integration of moral sentiments (emotions) and moral principles (reason). Social Customs vs. Philosophical Ethics: • Society's norms, customs, and legal laws shape individual consciences through family and culture. • Philosophical ethics requires stepping back from societal conditioning to critically evaluate our attitudes and sentiments. 👉 የሰው ልጅ ህሊና (Conscience) የተገነባው ከስሜት (Empathy/Sentiments) እና ከምክንያታዊ እውቀት (Moral Principles) ውህደት ነው። የህብረተሰብ ባህልና ህጎች ህሊናችንን ቢቀርጹትም፣ ፍልስፍናዊ ስነ-ምግባር ግን የራሳችንንና የህብረተሰቡን አስተሳሰብ በትኩረት እንድንመረምር ያስገድደናል። 💡 Exam Focus: Conscience = Moral Sentiments (emotions/empathy) + Moral Principles (reasoned analysis).

title: 3.3.2.1 Rationalisation in Ethical Arguments 🎭
content: 📌 Critical Reasoning in Ethics: • Moral arguments require solid, convincing reasons and explicit assumptions, not just personal opinions or a desire to "win" a debate. What is Rationalisation? • Definition: Using plausible, rational-sounding motives to disguise one's true (and often selfish/unconscious) motives. • Example: A landowner claiming to construct a factory to "create local jobs" when their real hidden motive is solely personal profit. • Genuine Reasoning: Openly acknowledging both profit and job creation as dual underlying motives. 👉 ራሽናላይዜሽን (Rationalisation) ማለት አንድ ሰው እውነተኛ (እና ምናልባትም ግልጽ ያልሆነ/ራስወዳድነት ያለው) ምክንያቱን ለመሸፈን ሲል አጥጋቢ የሚመስል የሽፍን ምክንያት ሲሰጥ ነው። በሞራል ክርክር ውስጥ ዋናው ዓላማ መረታት ሳይሆን እውነተኛና ምክንያታዊ መረዳት ላይ መድረስ ነው። 💡 Exam Hint: Rationalisation occurs when credible motives are used as a cover-up for actual underlying motives!

title: 3.3.2.2 Types of Reasoning in Moral Debates 📐
content: 📌 Three Main Forms of Critical Reasoning: 1. Reasoning by Analogy: • Explains a concept by comparing it to something similar. • Example: Comparing animal rights to human rights based on shared sentient characteristics. 2. Deductive Reasoning: • Applies a general universal principle to a specific situation. • Example: "If every human has human rights, and you are human, then you have human rights." 3. Inductive Reasoning: • Uses empirical evidence to support a general hypothesis. • Example: Accumulating scientific data on climate change to establish a moral duty to reduce emissions. 👉 በስነ-ምግባር ሙግት ውስጥ 3 የራሽናል አቀራረቦች አሉ፦ 1. በምሳሌ ማብራራት (Analogy): ሁለት ተመሳሳይ ነገሮችን በማወዳደር መሞገት። 2. ዲዳክቲቭ (Deductive): አጠቃላይ መርህን ወደ ተወሰነ ግለሰባዊ ሁኔታ ማውረድ። 3. ኢንዳክቲቭ (Inductive): በማስረጃዎችና መረጃዎች ላይ ተመስርቶ መደምደሚያ ላይ መድረስ። 💡 Exam Focus: Identify whether an argument uses Analogy (comparison), Deduction (general principle to specific case), or Induction (evidence to hypothesis)!

title: 3.3.2.3 Ethics and Religious Faith 🕊️
content: 📌 Faith-Based vs. Philosophical Ethics: • Religious View: Actions are right or wrong because they are commanded by God (Divine Command). • Philosophical Critique: If God commands an action because it is intrinsically right, rational reflection can discover rightness without divine command. Why Religious Arguments Matter in Ethics: • Rational consensus is rare; people disagree on fundamental moral truths. • Religious traditions possess powerful moral teachings that inspire public adherence to higher ethical standards. • Comprehensive ethical studies include faith arguments as relevant factors alongside rational analysis. 👉 በእምነት ላይ የተመሰረተ ሞራል ድርጊቶችን የፈጣሪ ትእዛዝ እንደሆኑ አድርጎ ያያል። በፍልስፍና እይታ ግን ሰው በምክንያታዊ አእምሮው ትክክለኛውን ነገር መለየት ይችላል። ሆኖም ግን ሃይማኖታዊ አስተምህሮዎች ሰፊውን ህብረተሰብ ወደ ላቀ የሞራል ደረጃ የማሸጋገር ትልቅ ሀይል ስላላቸው በኢቲክስ ጥናት ውስጥ አይገለሉም። 💡 Exam Hint: Philosophical ethics values rational reflection, but recognizes religious faith as a powerful catalyst for public moral standards.

title: 3.3.2.4 Three Criteria for Testing Moral Arguments 🧪
content: 📌 How to Evaluate and Test a Moral Argument: 1. Factual Accuracy: • David Hume argued you cannot derive an "ought" from an "is", but factual content remains vital. • Example: Opposing charity aid under the false claim that 90% goes to administration fails if facts prove 90% goes to the poor. 2. Consistency: • Moral judgments must be applied consistently unless a morally relevant difference exists. • Example: Claiming foreign debt of poor nations should be cancelled while refusing individual poor citizens' bank debt requires proving a relevant difference. 3. Good Will: • Arguments must exemplify genuine good intent, drawing on moral intuition and empathy. 👉 የአንድን የሞራል ሙግት ትክክለኛነት በ3 መንገዶች እንፈትሻለን፦ 1. የመረጃ ትክክለኛነት (Factual Accuracy): የቀረበው መረጃ ሀሰት ከሆነ ሞገቱ ይፈርሳል። 2. ወጥነት (Consistency): በተመሳሳይ ሁኔታዎች ላይ ተመሳሳይ የሞራል ውሳኔ መስጠት። 3. በጎ ፈቃድ (Good Will): ከልብ የሆነ በጎ አላማና እርህራሄን ማሳየት። 💡 Exam Focus: Memorize the 3 tests of moral arguments: Factual Accuracy, Consistency, and Good Will!

title: 3.3.3 Thinking Ethically: Framework for Decision Making 🛠️
content: 📌 The First Step in Moral Analysis: • Get the Facts: Crucial yet frequently overlooked. Facts tell us what is, though values are required to determine what ought to be. Five Framework Approaches to Ethical Decision-Making: 1. Fairness and Justice Approach 2. The Common Good Approach 3. The Rights Approach 4. The Utilitarian Approach 5. The Virtues Approach 👉 ማንኛውንም የስነ-ምግባር ውሳኔ ከመስጠታችን በፊት የመጀመሪያውና ዋናው እርምጃ መረጃዎችን (Facts) በትክክል ማሰባሰብ ነው። መረጃዎች ያሉበትን ሁኔታ የሚያሳዩ ሲሆን፣ እሴቶቻችን ደግሞ ሊሆን የሚገባውን ይነግሩናል። በኢቲክስ ውስጥ 5 ዋና ዋና አቀራረቦች አሉ። 💡 Exam Hint: "Getting the facts" is always the foundational first step before applying ethical values or frameworks.

title: 3.3.3.1 Fairness and Justice Approach ⚖️
content: 📌 Aristotelian Roots: • Rooted in Aristotle’s principle: "Equals should be treated equally and unequals unequally." • Rejects Favoritism (giving unwarranted benefits) and Discrimination (imposing unwarranted burdens). Aristotle's View on Moral Virtue & Happiness: • Ethics is practical knowledge (like sports or nutrition)—it requires actual practice to be virtuous. • Highest Good = Happiness: Achieved by fulfilling human function through reason (logos). Aristotle's 4 Categories of Humans: 1. The Virtuous 2. The Continent 3. The Incontinent 4. The Vicious 👉 ይህ አቀራረብ በነአርስቶትል ትምህርት ላይ የተመሰረተ ሲሆን፣ እኩል የሆኑ ሰዎች በእኩልነት፣ እኩል ያልሆኑ ደግሞ እንደ ልዩነታቸው መስተናገድ አለባቸው ይላል። አድልዎ (Favoritism) እና መድልዎ (Discrimination) ሁለቱም ኢ-ፍትሃዊ ናቸው። ሰዎችን ወደ 4 ይከፍላል፦ Virtuous, Continent, Incontinent እና Vicious። 💡 Exam Focus: Core Rule: Treat people the same unless there are morally relevant differences between them.

title: 3.3.3.2 The Common Good Approach 🤝
content: 📌 Core Concept: • Originating with Plato, Aristotle, and Cicero, and expanded by John Rawls. • Assumes individual wellbeing is inextricably linked to the wellbeing of the community. • John Rawls Definition: "Certain general conditions that are equally to everyone's advantage." Examples of Common Goods: • Affordable healthcare, effective public safety/police, just legal systems, public education, and an unpolluted environment. Ethical Principle: • "What is ethical is what advances the common good." 👉 የጋራ ጥቅም አቀራረብ በፕላቶ እና አርስቶትል የተጀመረ ሲሆን፣ የግለሰብ ደህንነት ከማህበረሰቡ ደህንነት ጋር የተሳሰረ ነው ይላል። እንደ ጤና ጥበቃ፣ ትምህርት፣ ሰላምና ንጹህ አካባቢ ያሉ ማህበረሰባዊ ሁኔታዎችን መጠበቅ የኢቲክስ ዋና አላማ ነው። 💡 Exam Hint: Focuses on societal conditions, institutions, and environments that serve everyone's shared welfare.

title: 3.3.3.3 The Rights Approach 🛡️
content: 📌 Kant’s Moral Foundation: • Based on Immanuel Kant's philosophy: Humans have dignity because they can freely choose their live path. • Humans are not objects to be manipulated; using people against their free choice violates human dignity. 4 Key Moral Rights: 1. Right to Truth: Right to be informed accurately about choices affecting us. 2. Right to Privacy: Right to personal beliefs and actions without interference. 3. Right Not to Be Injured: Protection from harm unless freely risking or deserving punishment. 4. Right to What Is Agreed: Right to fulfilled promises and contractual agreements. 👉 በኢማኑኤል ካንት ፍልስፍና የተመሰረተ ሲሆን፣ የሰው ልጅ ነፃ የመምረጥ መብትና ክብር አለው ይላል። ሰዎችን እንደ መጠቀሚያ ማድረግ ሰብአዊ ክብርን መጣስ ነው። ዋና ዋና መብቶች፦ የእውነት፣ የፕራይቬሲ፣ ያለመጎዳት እና የውል መብቶች ናቸው። 💡 Exam Focus: Actions are wrong to the extent that they violate individual rights and human dignity.

title: Ethical Problem Solving: 5 Guiding Questions ❓
content: 📌 Once all facts have been ascertained, apply these 5 key questions to resolve any moral issue: 1. Utilitarian Question: What benefits and harms will each action produce, and which leads to the best overall consequences? 2. Rights Question: What moral rights do affected parties have, and which action best respects those rights? 3. Justice Question: Which action treats everyone equally without unjustified favoritism or discrimination? 4. Common Good Question: Which course of action advances the overall common good of the community? 5. Virtue Question: Which course of action develops moral virtues in the decision-maker? 👉 ማንኛውንም የሞራል ችግር ለመፍታት መረጃ ከተሰበሰበ በኋላ እነዚህ 5 ጥያቄዎች ይጠየቃሉ፦ 1. የትኛው ውሳኔ የተሻለ ጥቅም/ውጤት ያመጣል? (Utilitarian) 2. የትኛው ውሳኔ የመብት መከበርን ያረጋግጣል? (Rights) 3. የትኛው ውሳኔ ፍትሃዊና አድልዎ የሌለው ነው? (Fairness/Justice) 4. የትኛው ውሳኔ የጋራ ጥቅምን ያሳድጋል? (Common Good) 5. የትኛው ውሳኔ በጎ ምግባርን ያጎለብታል? (Virtues) 💡 Exam Focus: Memorize these 5 questions as the complete framework for resolving ethical dilemmas on exams! --- 🎯 ❤️ ውዶች፣ ይህንን ክፍል በተሳካ ሁኔታ አጠናቀናል። የለፋችሁበትና የደከማችሁበት ሁሉ አምሮና አብቦ በከፍተኛ ውጤት እንደምትካሱ ከልቤ አምናለሁ! አምላክ ጥረታችሁን ይባርክ፤ በፈተናችሁ ላይም ብሩህ አእምሮንና መረጋጋትን ይስጣችሁ። ሁሌም ትልቅ ደረጃ ደርሳችሁ ለማየት ጉጉት አለኝ። መልካም እድልና ስኬት ከእኔ ወንድማዊ አክብሮትና ፍቅር ጋር!
